text: Sources: Poland case, p. 305; European Commission, Poland forecast, 21 May 2026

This case is about a Canadian company planning to make power tools near Warsaw.

First, Poland looks attractive because of its skilled workers and good transport. Today, higher energy costs and finding enough staff are concerns.

Second, the company is using an economic approach. It expects lower costs and hopes to make a profit by selling tools across the region.

Before investing, it should talk to buyers, compare competitors and prices, and check costs and local rules. This would help it avoid spending money on a factory without enough customers.

To succeed, it needs reliable tools, affordable prices and local sales and repair support. I would start small and test demand before expanding.

Sources
Local case: In the International Spotlight: Poland, page 305, course PDF. The scenario contains figures from 2012. The proposed investment and expected lower costs are case assumptions, not independently verified current market facts.
2026 update for Question 1: European Commission, Economic forecast for Poland, 21 May 2026. https://economy-finance.ec.europa.eu/economic-surveillance-eu-member-states/country-pages-including-country-reports/poland/economic-forecast-poland_en
Question 3: environmental scanning means gathering and checking information about customers, competitors, costs and rules before deciding. Question 2 uses an economic imperative approach; political incentives and product quality support the plan but are not its main motive.
